subject: environmental-science
title: Mitigation Hierarchy
welcome_lead: Avoid first. Then reduce. Then remediate. Last resort: offset.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on the mitigation hierarchy in EIA.
final_note: Offsetting comes last — never as an excuse to skip earlier steps.

concepts.def: Sequential approach: avoid → minimise → remediate → offset.
Re-routing or redesigning to prevent impact entirely.
Reducing duration, intensity or extent of unavoidable impacts.
Compensating residual impacts via equivalent gains elsewhere.
Policy goal of balancing residual losses with offsets so total impact = 0.

walkthroughs.body_html: Each step is more expensive and less certain than the last. Avoidance is cheapest and most reliable.
Offsets must be additional, equivalent or better, and permanent — challenging for unique habitats.
UK 2021 Environment Act mandates 10% biodiversity net gain in planning, going beyond no net loss.
